blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Many of the people killed in the ruthless drug war waged by former President Rodrigo Duterte were breadwinners who worked blue-collar jobs and came from slum communities. The stories of how they were victimized and suffered from the extrajudicial killings will be heard when Duterte’s trial for crimes against humanity in the International Criminal Court (ICC) begins on Nov. 30. The common legal representatives of victims (CLRVs) identified the profile of the 539 people admitted as “victims” in Duterte’s case.
